description: Research Experiences for Undergraduates (REU), NHERI 2022: Deep Learning-based Friction Modeling of Dry Interfaces for Structural Dampers is a dataset listed in DesignSafe Data Depot (published projects), a research data repository for natural hazards engineering under the section "other", published or maintained by James Ricles, Lehigh University (lehigh.edu). This project develops a physics-informed friction model to describe a rotary friction damper. A LuGre friction model is augmented using online parameter updating to capture semi-active and backlash effects. The methodology given here can be applied in general to friction systems. Coverage: as described in the project (site or event named in the description). DesignSafe files it as a "other" project. Its DOI is 10.17603/ds2-p659-3295. Keywords: NHERI Lehigh; natural hazards; friction dampers; friction modeling; physics-informed machine learning; LuGre model. Published 2022-08-12. It is reached through the links recorded on this page, with the catalogue entry as the discovery route. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is CC-BY-4.0 (labelled "Creative Commons Attribution" on the DesignSafe project). Caveats: this record was written from the catalogue listing only, so the linked page was not opened, its contents and current availability were not checked, and the description may lag the source. It can support structural performance, hazard exposure and resilience studies. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-designsafe-data-depot-repository.
